message.reasoning_content: We need to determine appropriate crime(s) based on facts. The person is a deputy director of environmental protection bureau, a public official, who signed false documents certifying project completion, leading to illegal disbursement of public funds. This is classic abuse of power and embezzlement? Likely "滥用职权" (abuse of power) and "挪用公款" (misappropriation of public funds) or "受贿"? He didn't receive bribes, he caused extra funds to be paid to a company. That's "滥用职权" (abuse of power) and "挪用公款" maybe "职务侵占"? Actually, the official used his position to cause the government to pay funds that were not due. That is "滥用职权" (abuse of power) and possibly "贪污" (embezzlement) because he caused the state to pay money to a company, but the official didn't personally receive money? The facts: he signed false reports, leading to extra 116.21 million? Actually 116.21 thousand? The amount is 116.21万元. He may be liable for "滥用职权" and "挪用公款" if he appropriated funds. But the text says "致使...多得国家专项资金116.21万元". He didn't necessarily take the money himself. Could be "滥用职权" and "徇私舞弊"? In Chinese criminal law, "滥用职权罪" (abuse of power) is for public officials who abuse authority causing state losses. Also "职务侵占罪" (embezzlement) is for officials who appropriate public funds for personal use. Here he didn't appropriate for personal use, just approved false completion leading to payment to a company. That is "滥用职权罪" (abuse of power) and possibly "受贿罪"? No bribe. So answer likely "滥用职权". In examples, they sometimes list multiple crimes separated by semicolon. For similar case: earlier example about 贪污 (embezzlement) for officials who misused funds. Here it's not personal gain. So "滥用职权". Could also be "职务侵占"? But that requires personal appropriation. Not present. So answer: [罪名]滥用职权<eoa>.
